top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises one clearly owned invention (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) and its decisive realization (Ye's strontium clock at about 1e-18, including control of many-body effects), reproduced independently at several institutions, with a two-name allocation that matches the division of labour and a citation that separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is mature and conceptually important but has an unresolved credit gap (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D generalisation) and is better than no award only because its science is well confirmed.
recusal_note: P001 lies in my own subfield of atomic physics and precision spectroscopy, but my profile documents no collaboration with Katori or Ye; no specific recusal apparent from profile. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) has no documented connection.
